paper_id: Li et al. - 2010 - Multicast Capacity of Wireless Ad Hoc Networks Under Gaussian Channel Model
title: Multicast Capacity of Wireless Ad Hoc Networks Under Gaussian Channel Model
motivation: Need to understand asymptotic achievable throughput when Θ(n) wireless nodes are randomly deployed in a given region for multicast sessions
problem_framing: Model random Poisson network with constant power P, path loss α>2, Gaussian channel; find per-flow multicast capacity scaling with n, n_s, and k
key_insight: Use percolation theory to construct highway system enabling optimal per-flow multicast rate Θ(1/√(nk)) in random networks
method_signature: Bond percolation on grid creates open paths forming highways; construct Euclidean spanning trees to relay multicast data
evaluation_criteria: Minimum per-flow multicast throughput λ_k(n) achievable w.h.p.; compare lower bound vs upper bound O(√n/(n_s√k))
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: We do not know whether the boundary on k is tight; the boundary most likely is not tight; hidden constants in all formulas are not tight
evidence_for_taste: we do not know whether the boundary on k is tight
we think that the boundary most likely is not tight
A more careful analysis will further narrow the difference
the hidden constants in all our formulas are not tight
We leave it as a future work to study the scenario when network coding is permitted
thinking_moves: Extend unicast percolation result to multicast by building spanning trees over highway system
Compare Gaussian channel model with protocol model results to identify gap
Prove lower bound via constructive routing, then derive matching upper bound via information-theoretic constraints
Identify that increasing receivers only decreases throughput by 1/√k factor
Admit uncertainty about tightness of scaling threshold k=O(n/log^{2α+6}n)
